tax_treatment: A Mexican company pays 30% corporate income tax plus 10% mandatory employee profit sharing. Dividends to the UK parent bear 10% withholding. Intercompany flows need transfer pricing documentation. VAT of 16% on sales is recoverable.
liability_and_exit: Liability is limited to the subsidiary capital, but the group carries local employment and tax-audit exposure. Exit is by share sale or liquidation, which needs tax authority clearance and usually takes 6 to 12 months.

tax_treatment: Royalties received from the Mexican franchisee are taxable in the UK; Mexico withholds 10% under the UK-Mexico treaty (25% without treaty relief) and VAT of 16% applies to the royalty. No transfer pricing filing unless the franchisee is a related party.
liability_and_exit: The franchisee bears operating and employment liabilities; the group keeps brand, product and IP indemnity risk. Exit is by termination under the franchise agreement; with too much control over operations there is a risk of creating a taxable presence in Mexico.
